Figure 2:Overview of DRBench Pro.(A)We construct a Wikipedia-derived local graph around a selected root entity and sample subgraphs by retaining selected children of the root and their complete descendant subtrees together with the root.(B1)Each sampled subgraph defines a research query.(B2)Each sampled edge is converted into an edge-grounded rubric, forming the hidden rubric set.(C)An evaluated deep research agent answers the query with a report; a judge scores the report against the rubric set, and the edge-level scores are mapped back to the local knowledge tree and aggregated bottom-up into breadth and depth.

Figure 7:Research-process profiles under the local research framework: (a) final-report length, (b) issued Search calls, (c) unique retrieved Wikipedia pages, (d) issued Open calls, (e) Gap Unit incidence, and (f) source-ID-valid citation markers. Dashed lines mark the mean of the seven displayed backbone-LLM means.

Figure 11:Local research framework workflow.The backbone LLM decomposes the research query into three Research Units, which execute concurrently against the shared frozen Wikipedia snapshot throughSearchandOpen. Their evidence notes undergo one coverage-gap check; when a material gap is found, at most one Gap Unit collects supplemental evidence before the original query and all collected notes are synthesized into the final report.
